message: Published research from dated official evidence, reviewed through the Codex subscription. No runtime model generation.

data.headline: A flatter Treasury curve and firmer overnight funding.
data.summary: The latest collected observations disagree across maturities: the two-year Treasury yield rose while ten- and thirty-year yields fell. Overnight secured funding subsequently edged higher. Keep these differently dated inputs separate from current equity prices; they do not establish a complete morning trading verdict.

bull.text: The ten-year yield fell from 4.94% on October 30 to 4.91% on November 2; the thirty-year yield fell from 5.31% to 5.28%. Lower long yields can ease one valuation constraint, but these observations do not measure an equity-market response.

bear.text: The two-year yield rose from 4.56% to 4.59% over the same dates. SOFR rose from 3.95% on November 2 to 3.97% on November 3. These are separate Treasury and secured-funding observations, not a new central-bank policy decision.

watch.text: Overnight reverse-repo usage fell from $5.087 billion to $0.427 billion on November 3. The $4.660 billion decline does not establish that money entered equities or quantify total market liquidity.
October 27 S&P futures asset managers were net long 923,449 contracts while leveraged funds were net short 400,604. This older category disagreement cannot identify the present price trend.

limitations: Treasury yields describe November 2; SOFR and reverse-repo figures describe November 3. These are delayed official observations, not live prices or the market response to a release.
CFTC figures are October 27 futures-only category positions. Related futures differ from ETF shares and do not identify current purchases, fund flows or individual investors.
Current ETF prices, option chains, gamma, representative social sentiment and dark-pool direction remain independently unmeasured. Hosted displays are separate from saved evidence.
The interpretation describes possible transmission channels, not measured causation, a return prediction or a calibrated trading probability. No prospective model is qualified.
